explanation_en: 'Dar un respiro' (or 'tener un respiro') means to provide or have a temporary relief, pause, or break from a difficult situation (like heat, work, or stress). 'Respiro' literally means 'breath'. It is a very common idiomatic expression in everyday conversations and news reports.

examples.en_text: After working ten hours straight, I can finally take a breather.
examples.target_text: Después de trabajar diez horas seguidas, por fin puedo tomarme un respiro.

examples.en_text: The drop in gasoline prices will give families a breather this month.
examples.target_text: La bajada de los precios de la gasolina dará un respiro a las familias este mes.

examples.en_text: It looks like the rain is going to give us a break this weekend.
examples.target_text: Parece que la lluvia nos va a dar un respiro este fin de semana.

examples.en_text: I need a breather; the kids have been screaming all afternoon.
examples.target_text: Necesito un respiro; los niños han estado gritando toda la tarde.

examples.en_text: This short vacation has served as a temporary relief from daily stress.
examples.target_text: Estas vacaciones cortas me han servido para tener un respiro del estrés diario.

examples.en_text: The boss gave us a break and postponed the project deadline.
examples.target_text: El jefe nos dio un respiro y pospuso la fecha límite del proyecto.

explanation_en: Literally meaning 'in the heart of,' this expression is used both geographically and metaphorically to refer to the central, most vital part of something. In political or administrative contexts, it highlights the core hub of operations or the essence of an issue. It is highly common in formal speeches, news, and essays.

examples.en_text: Living in the heart of Madrid is expensive, but you have everything nearby.
examples.target_text: Vivir en el corazón de Madrid es caro, pero tienes todo cerca.

examples.en_text: The debate on climate change is at the heart of current politics.
examples.target_text: El debate sobre el cambio climático está en el corazón de la política actual.

examples.en_text: They found a beautiful cabin in the heart of the forest.
examples.target_text: Encontraron una cabaña preciosa en el corazón del bosque.

examples.en_text: Customer service must be at the heart of our business strategy.
examples.target_text: El servicio al cliente debe estar en el corazón de nuestra estrategia empresarial.

examples.en_text: The music festival is held every year in the heart of the city.
examples.target_text: El festival de música se celebra cada año en el corazón de la ciudad.

examples.en_text: Mutual trust is at the heart of a lasting friendship.
examples.target_text: La confianza mutua está en el corazón de una amistad duradera.

explanation_en: A very common transitional phrase meaning 'as a result of' or 'consequent to.' It is preferred in formal, journalistic, and academic registers over simpler alternatives like 'por' or 'debido a.' It is always followed by a noun phrase.

examples.en_text: As a result of the heavy rains, the train was delayed by two hours.
examples.target_text: Como consecuencia de las fuertes lluvias, el tren se retrasó dos horas.

examples.en_text: The company had to close two stores as a result of the economic crisis.
examples.target_text: La empresa tuvo que cerrar dos tiendas como consecuencia de la crisis económica.

examples.en_text: He lost a lot of weight as a result of a healthy diet and daily exercise.
examples.target_text: Perdió mucho peso como consecuencia de una dieta saludable y ejercicio diario.

examples.en_text: As a result of the new privacy policy, many users closed their accounts.
examples.target_text: Como consecuencia de la nueva política de privacidad, muchos usuarios cerraron sus cuentas.

examples.en_text: Her Spanish level improved quickly as a result of her study trip to Madrid.
examples.target_text: Su nivel de español mejoró rápidamente como consecuencia de su viaje de estudios a Madrid.

examples.en_text: Traffic in the center has improved as a result of the construction of new subway lines.
examples.target_text: El tráfico en el centro ha mejorado como consecuencia de la construcción de nuevas líneas de metro.

explanation_en: This fixed prepositional formula means 'at the request of' or 'by demand of.' It is widely used in administrative, legal, and formal contexts to indicate who initiated an action. It is followed by a person, group, or institution.

examples.en_text: The pianist played another song at the request of the audience.
examples.target_text: El pianista tocó otra canción a petición del público.

examples.en_text: We organized the meeting in the afternoon at the request of the boss.
examples.target_text: Organizamos la reunión por la tarde a petición de la jefa.

examples.en_text: The document was modified at the request of the clients.
examples.target_text: El documento fue modificado a petición de los clientes.

examples.en_text: The teacher changed the exam date at the request of the students.
examples.target_text: El profesor cambió la fecha del examen a petición de los alumnos.

examples.en_text: We prepared a special dinner at the request of my grandmother.
examples.target_text: Preparamos una cena especial a petición de mi abuela.

examples.en_text: The city council planted more trees at the request of the neighbors.
examples.target_text: El ayuntamiento plantó más árboles a petición de los vecinos.

explanation_en: A versatile prepositional phrase meaning 'along' (spatial) or 'throughout / over the course of' (temporal). For advanced learners, mastering its temporal use (e.g., 'a lo largo de la historia') is crucial for writing cohesive essays and understanding historical or news narratives.

examples.en_text: He has worked in different companies throughout his professional career.
examples.target_text: Ha trabajado en diferentes empresas a lo largo de su carrera profesional.

examples.en_text: There is a very nice path to walk along the river.
examples.target_text: Hay un camino muy bonito para caminar a lo largo del río.

examples.en_text: We have had some technical problems throughout the year, but they are already resolved.
examples.target_text: Hemos tenido algunos problemas técnicos a lo largo del año, pero ya están resueltos.

examples.en_text: People change their minds throughout their lives.
examples.target_text: Las personas cambian de opinión a lo largo de la vida.

examples.en_text: Throughout the meeting, we will analyze the details of the new project.
examples.target_text: A lo largo de la reunión, iremos analizando los detalles del nuevo proyecto.

examples.en_text: They placed informative posters along the main avenue.
examples.target_text: Colocaron carteles informativos a lo largo de la avenida principal.

explanation_en: This expression means 'in charge of,' 'under the responsibility of,' or 'run by.' It is used to designate leadership or duty over a task, department, or event. It is a key collocation in professional and administrative Spanish.

examples.en_text: The new marketing project is being run by Sofía.
examples.target_text: El nuevo proyecto de marketing está a cargo de Sofía.

examples.en_text: My older brother was left in charge of the house while my parents were away on a trip.
examples.target_text: Mi hermano mayor quedó a cargo de la casa mientras mis padres estaban de viaje.

examples.en_text: The organization of the charity event is run by a group of volunteers.
examples.target_text: La organización del evento benéfico está a cargo de un grupo de voluntarios.

examples.en_text: Who is in charge of the customer service department?
examples.target_text: ¿Quién está a cargo del departamento de atención al cliente?

examples.en_text: The theater workshop will be run by a professional actor.
examples.target_text: El taller de teatro estará a cargo de un actor profesional.

examples.en_text: Don't worry about the food, I'll take charge of the kitchen tonight.
examples.target_text: No te preocupes por la comida, yo me quedo a cargo de la cocina esta noche.

explanation_en: An emphatic variation of 'sin duda,' meaning 'without any doubt whatsoever.' The addition of 'alguna' (placed after the noun 'duda') reinforces the certainty. It is a great rhetorical tool to sound more persuasive and native in both spoken and written Spanish.

examples.en_text: It is, without a doubt, the best decision we have made this year.
examples.target_text: Es, sin duda alguna, la mejor decisión que hemos tomado este año.

examples.en_text: If you are going to travel to Galicia, without a doubt you have to bring an umbrella.
examples.target_text: Si vas a viajar a Galicia, sin duda alguna tienes que llevar un paraguas.

examples.en_text: She is, without a doubt, the most qualified person for the manager position.
examples.target_text: Ella es, sin duda alguna, la persona más calificada para el puesto de gerente.

examples.en_text: This restaurant has, without a doubt, the best croquettes in the city.
examples.target_text: Este restaurante tiene, sin duda alguna, las mejores croquetas de la ciudad.

examples.en_text: Learning another language will, without a doubt, open many doors for you in the future.
examples.target_text: Aprender otro idioma te abrirá, sin duda alguna, muchas puertas en el futuro.

examples.en_text: The team played very well and, without a doubt, deserved to win the match.
examples.target_text: El equipo jugó muy bien y, sin duda alguna, merecía ganar el partido.

explanation_en: Borrowed from the English 'ground zero', this term is widely used in Spanish to refer to the epicenter of a disaster, tragedy, or major event. It is common in journalistic contexts and news reports. It is always used with the feminine article 'la'.

examples.en_text: The earthquake destroyed almost all the buildings at ground zero.
examples.target_text: El terremoto destruyó casi todos los edificios en la zona cero.

examples.en_text: The tourists visited the monument built at ground zero.
examples.target_text: Los tourists visitaron el monumento construido en la zona cero.

examples.en_text: This market was considered ground zero for the outbreak of the disease.
examples.target_text: Este mercado fue considerado la zona cero del brote de la enfermedad.

examples.en_text: The industrial neighborhood became ground zero for unemployment in the city.
examples.target_text: El barrio industrial se convirtió en la zona cero del desempleo en la ciudad.

examples.en_text: The firefighters are still working to put out the fire at ground zero.
examples.target_text: Los bomberos todavía están trabajando para apagar el fuego en la zona cero.

examples.en_text: No one was able to survive the explosion at ground zero.
examples.target_text: Nadie pudo sobrevivir a la explosión en la zona cero.

explanation_en: While 'quedarse con' literally means 'to keep' something, in this context it is used idiomatically to mean 'to remember', 'to note', or 'to pay attention to' a piece of information. It is highly colloquial and very common in spoken Spanish when highlighting a key detail.

examples.en_text: If you have to choose just one idea from the meeting, keep this one in mind: we have to reduce costs.
examples.target_text: Si tienes que elegir una sola idea de la reunión, quédate con esta: tenemos que reducir los costes.

examples.en_text: From today's whole class, remember the rule for irregular verbs; the rest is secondary.
examples.target_text: De toda la clase de hoy, quédate con la regla de los verbos irregulares; lo demás es secundario.

examples.en_text: To make a good sauce, keep this trick in mind: always add a little sugar at the end.
examples.target_text: Para hacer una buena salsa, quédate con este truco: añade siempre un poco de azúcar al final.

examples.en_text: If you are going to travel to that country, remember the name of this app to get around the city.
examples.target_text: Si vas a viajar a ese país, quédate con el nombre de esta aplicación para moverte por la ciudad.

examples.en_text: Don't worry about all the details of the speech, keep in mind the main message we want to convey.
examples.target_text: No te preocupes por todos los detalles del discurso, quédate con el mensaje principal que queremos transmitir.

examples.en_text: If you read this article, keep the second paragraph in mind, which is where the real problem is explained.
examples.target_text: Si lees este artículo, quédate con el segundo párrafo, que es donde se explica el problema real.

explanation_en: This verbal collocation means 'to make clear' or 'to clarify'. The adjective 'claro' must agree with the direct object if it is explicit, but when used with a pronoun like 'lo' or as a general statement, it remains masculine singular. It is used in both formal and informal registers to emphasize a point.

examples.en_text: The boss made it clear in the meeting: we cannot arrive late.
examples.target_text: El jefe lo dejó claro en la reunión: no podemos llegar tarde.

examples.en_text: I don't want there to be any misunderstandings, that's why I prefer to make it clear from the beginning.
examples.target_text: No quiero que haya malentendidos, por eso prefiero dejarlo claro desde el principio.

examples.en_text: She made it clear that she has no intention of changing her mind.
examples.target_text: Ella dejó claro que no tiene intención de cambiar de opinión.

examples.en_text: Do you think I've made it clear, or should I explain it again?
examples.target_text: ¿Crees que lo he dejado claro o debería explicarlo otra vez?

examples.en_text: We already made it clear last week, so we are not going to repeat the same thing.
examples.target_text: Nosotros ya lo dejamos claro la semana pasada, así que no vamos a repetir lo mismo.

examples.en_text: It's important that you make clear what you expect from this project.
examples.target_text: Es importante que dejes claro lo que esperas de este proyecto.

explanation_en: The structure 'dejar de + infinitive' means 'to stop doing something'. When combined with 'ser', it means 'to stop being' a certain way or thing. In this sentence, 'lo' refers back to 'pueblo fantasma', demonstrating a common Spanish syntactic pattern of using object pronouns to replace predicate nouns.

examples.en_text: If this job stops being interesting, I will look for another one.
examples.target_text: Si este trabajo deja de ser interesante, buscaré otro.

examples.en_text: After that argument, they stopped being friends.
examples.target_text: Después de esa discusión, ellos dejaron de ser amigos.

examples.en_text: Learning languages will never stop being useful.
examples.target_text: Aprender idiomas nunca dejará de ser útil.

examples.en_text: We must stop being so hard on ourselves.
examples.target_text: Debemos dejar de ser tan duros con nosotros mismos.

examples.en_text: I have stopped being so shy since I started working in customer service.
examples.target_text: He dejado de ser tan tímido desde que trabajo en atención al cliente.

examples.en_text: If you stop being so impatient, you will see that everything will turn out well.
examples.target_text: Si dejas de ser tan impaciente, verás que todo saldrá bien.

explanation_en: This idiomatic expression literally translates to 'at skin level' and is used to describe emotions that are very close to the surface, highly visible, or easily triggered. It is commonly paired with nouns like 'emociones', 'nervios', or 'sentimientos'. It is an excellent B2/C1 expression for describing intense emotional states.

examples.en_text: After watching that sad movie, my emotions are right on the surface.
examples.target_text: Después de ver esa película tan triste, tengo las emociones a flor de piel.

examples.en_text: Before the final exam, all the students' nerves were on edge.
examples.target_text: Antes del examen final, todos los estudiantes tenían los nervios a flor de piel.

examples.en_text: At my sister's wedding, feelings were running high and many people cried.
examples.target_text: En la boda de mi hermana, los sentimientos estaban a flor de piel y muchos lloraron.

examples.en_text: Don't say anything to him today; he's had a bad day and is highly sensitive.
examples.target_text: No le digas nada hoy; ha tenido un mal día y tiene la sensibilidad a flor de piel.

examples.en_text: During the last minute of the match, the tension was palpable in the stadium.
examples.target_text: Durante el último minuto del partido, la tensión estaba a flor de piel en el estadio.

examples.en_text: I love how she sings; you can tell she wears her passion on her sleeve.
examples.target_text: Me encanta cómo canta ella, se nota que transmite su pasión a flor de piel.
